sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:38

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:38:1
items.html:
Bina did not turn her face to illuminate downward in Hesed, for there was no power, etc.: And you must know that there are here in Bina three lights. The first is the light of the male that she received from the refinement of the male of Hochma, which is phase two. The second is the aspect of the record of the vessel of Bina herself, such as there is in each and every vessel from the time of the first expansion, and this is regarded as the aspect of the female of Bina. The third is the light of Hesed, that is, the level of ZA, which she now received from the remainder of the refinement of phase two of the vessel of Hochma; and this is regarded as the aspect of the son of Bina, and is not at all of the aspect of the light of Bina. And this third light is called VAK [six ends], whose meaning is that it lacks the illumination of GAR, that is, the light of Hochma, and there is in it nothing but the aspect of Hassadim alone.
And this is what he says, “Bina did not turn her face to illuminate downward in Hesed, for there was no power in Hesed and in VAK to receive so great a light face to face.” For since the light of Hesed is now in Katnut [smallness], that is, the light of Hassadim alone, entirely without the illumination of GAR, since it emerges from a coupling on a screen of phase one, in which there is no illumination of Hochma, it therefore has no power to receive anything from Bina and to descend and clothe in the vessels of VAK. Therefore it remained still in the vessel of Bina and did not expand to the vessel of Hesed.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:38:2
items.html: The seven lower lights were nullified with respect to her light. That is, although Bina received the light of Hesed into herself, which is the light of the seven lower Sefirot, which lack GAR, as above, she nevertheless did not thereby lose the light of her own GAR, since the light of the seven lower ones is nullified in her with respect to her own great light, which are her male and Nukva, which are of phase two, as above.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:38:3
items.html: And the light of Hochma, although its light is greater than her light, etc. This refers to the male of the vessel of Bina, which she received through the refinement of the male of the vessel of Hochma (as above in item 35), and it is called the light of Hochma because the matter of refinement spoken of with respect to the male of Hochma is the aspect of a coupling between the male and the Nukva of Hochma, from whose coupling together the light of the male of Bina was born. For the Nukva of the vessel of Hochma has a level of phase two, as above, and the male of Hochma has a level of phase three; therefore, when the male refined from phase three to phase two, it turns out that it equalized its level with that of its Nukva, and then both of them were included together in a joint screen of phase two, and a coupling by striking was made upon it, and a new level of phase two emerged, joint from male and female together. And this new level is the one that descended and became the male in the vessel of Bina. And you find that this male of the vessel of Bina is of a level equal with the female of the vessel of Hochma, and it is therefore called the light of Hochma. And this is what he says, “and she is able to receive the light of Hochma,” that is, her aspect of the male, as explained, whose level is equal to the light of Bina that is in the vessel of Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:38:4
items.html: Aba and Ima dwell as one. For even Bina of direct light is discerned as the very essence of Hochma of direct light. And all the more so here, where Hochma too has only the level of Bina, as above.
